title: Networking, persistence and scale for a shared persistent world in 2026
summary: Live-searched landscape brief (20/20 searches, extracts only; no page fetches) on networking, persistence and scale for a persistent user-created world in 2026. Verified: Star Citizen's static meshing gives ~500-player shards and, as of CIG's 27 Aug 2026 letter, dynamic meshing exists only as "quasi-dynamic" instancing in 4.10; EVE's real single-system record is 6,739 pilots (M2-XFE) under time dilation; Improbable's 10k figure is a 2022 capability claim with observed peaks of ~4,100-4,500 at scripted events and no 2024-25 10k event found; Dual Universe's single shard shut down 27 Aug 2025; Roblox's public ceiling is 200/server with 700 as a now-closed beta, with DataStore budgets of 60+10xplayers req/min; Fortnite stays at <=100 per instance (Big Battle is 40v40/50v50); Unreal Iris is still opt-in/experimental. Infrastructure prices have converged at ~US$0.055-0.07 per vCPU-hour (GameLift c6i.large US$0.109/h; Edgegap US$0.00115/vCPU-min + US$0.10/GB), i.e. ~US$0.002-0.005 per avatar-hour, but vendor risk is now the dominant risk: Hathora was acquired by Fireworks AI and wound down game hosting by Apr/May 2026, Dolby.io Communications is quietly legacy, and Linden Lab closed Firestorm Zero by mid-2025 after its streaming provider forced a migration. Voice and netcode are cheap and commoditised (Photon 100 CCU free, Fusion 2 >200/room; ODIN EUR0.29/PCU-month; Discord Social SDK free, GA Aug 2025). Recommended: two-layer presence/simulation model with elastic cells of 100-150 simulated avatars, 500-1,000 per contiguous place, 2,000-5,000 only in a degraded event mode, multi-vendor hosting and voice abstractions, document+event-log persistence with write budgets, and moderation budgeted before capacity.
design_implications: Adopt a two-layer world model: a low-rate presence layer (position, pose, voice, chat at 5-10 Hz, interest-managed) that can show 1,000-5,000 avatars per place, and a spatially sharded simulation layer with cells of 50-150 physically interacting avatars.

Set published 2026 concurrency SLOs per place: 100-150 fully simulated avatars per cell with voice; 500-1,000 per contiguous multi-cell place (the Star Citizen 4.x shard envelope); 2,000-5,000 only in a declared event mode with impostors, pre-mixed audio and reduced interaction (the ScavLab envelope); never promise 10,000.
Use elastic cells backed by an authoritative replication/entity store so a cell crash is a reconnect, not a lost place; sell land by area and content budget, never by 'one server'.

Design for vendor churn: containerised cell servers deployable on Edgegap, GameLift Servers, Nitrado GameFabric or bare metal from one manifest; voice behind an abstraction that can swap ODIN, Discord Social SDK or a self-hosted SFU; no sole-source streaming client (Hathora, Dolby.io and Firestorm Zero all disappeared within 12-18 months).

Budget infrastructure at roughly US$0.002-0.005 per avatar-hour (US$0.055-0.07/vCPU-hour, US$0.10/GB) and voice at about EUR0.29 per peak user per month; expect trust-and-safety and asset moderation, not servers, to be the largest operating line.

Persist world state as documents plus an append-only event log with Roblox-style per-cell and per-creator write budgets, snapshots and rollback for land owners; keep live world state out of simulation memory.
Sandbox scripts (Luau or WASM) with per-script CPU/memory/network budgets and throttle the worst offender rather than starving all scripts as Second Life does.
Treat interest management, avatar LOD/impostors beyond ~30 m and a 50-200 kbps per-client bandwidth cap as the primary scale levers; if on Unreal, use Iris only as an experimental opt-in.
Make instance boundaries soft (friends-follow, join-where-my-people-are, cross-instance chat, auto-merge thin instances) rather than chasing bigger instances.
Use pixel streaming only as a time-capped onboarding funnel with a provider contract that survives platform migrations.
open_questions: Which Star Citizen 4.x patch is live in October 2026, whether 4.10 instancing has expanded beyond quasi-dynamic meshing, and the current official per-shard player count.
Whether Roblox's 700-player server tier will re-open publicly and what Luau CPU budget per player it implies.
Whether any independently measured MSquared/Morpheus event in 2024-2026 reached 10k concurrent, with update rate, avatar fidelity and per-attendee cost.
The official Dolby.io Communications API end-of-service date and which spatial-voice vendor (ODIN, Vivox, Discord) absorbed its customers.
Nitrado GameFabric's post-Hathora rate card and whether Edgegap's US$0.00115/vCPU-min holds into 2027.
Whether Unreal Iris leaves Experimental in UE 5.8+ and what per-server player gain Epic attributes to it.
Linden Lab's actual AWS spend versus the pre-2020 colocation bill, and whether Project Zero (as distinct from Firestorm Zero) is still operating.
Whether a WebGPU client can render a 100-avatar presence layer at 60 fps on 2026 mid-range phones.

claims.claim: As of CIG's 27 August 2026 Letter from the Chairman, Star Citizen's dynamic server meshing has shipped only as 'Quasi Dynamic Server Meshing' (instancing in Alpha 4.10); persistent-universe territories are not yet subdivided by load. Alpha 4.0 static meshing raised shard capacity to roughly 500 players.

EVE Online's verified single-system peak is 6,739 pilots in M2-XFE (breaking FWST-8's 6,557), with 13,770 across three systems; the '8,825 players' figure in the prior draft does not appear in CCP's reports.

Improbable's 'over 10,000 participants in one space' is a 2022 capability claim; observed peaks are 4,144 real players (ScavLab, May 2021) and 4,500 (Yuga Labs demo). Two searches found no 2024-2025 MSquared event with 10k+ concurrent users.

Hathora, a leading game-server hosting vendor, was acquired by Fireworks AI (announced March 2026) and wound down game hosting by end of April/May 2026, offboarding customers to Nitrado GameFabric; Stormgate lost online play as a result.

Edgegap charges US$0.00115 per dedicated vCPU-minute (~US$0.069/vCPU-hour, raised from US$0.001 on 1 Jan 2025) plus US$0.10/GB egress; Amazon GameLift Servers lists c6i.large at US$0.109/hour Linux on-demand in US East (Ohio).
Dual Universe's single-shard MMO was delisted from Steam on 25 July 2025 and its servers shut down on 27 August 2025, surviving only as the player-hosted 'myDU'.

Roblox's public maximum server size is 200 players (since 24 July 2024, per a secondary source); a 700-player tier existed as a beta that developers report can no longer be joined publicly. Official DataStore budgets are 60 + 10 x players requests/minute per server with a 30-request per-key queue.

Photon's free tier is now 100 CCU for commercial Fusion/Quantum apps, Fusion 2 supports over 200 players in a room; ODIN spatial voice costs EUR0.29 per peak concurrent user per month (free to 25 CCU); Discord's Social SDK with in-game voice went GA to all developers free in August 2025.

Linden Lab's Firestorm Zero streamed viewer (launched 14 March 2025) was shut down by June 2025 because of the cost of maintaining two streaming products and a provider-mandated platform migration of Project Zero.

Unreal's Iris replication remains opt-in alongside legacy replication and is reported still marked Experimental in UE 5.7 documentation; Fortnite's standard instance remains 100 players and Big Battle is a 40v40/50v50 LTM, not a larger single place.
